purpose: Primary-source claim ledger for the historical Fresnel-series explainer film.

scope.animationEvidence: Synthetic CAD motion explains research concepts; it is not measured hardware telemetry or a perceptual result.

sources.title: FresnelShape: A Contact-Plane Tilt Haptic Display for Enhancing Visuo-Haptic Coherence
sources.inspected: Publisher's complete featured abstract and publication metadata.
sources.scopeLimit: Only publisher-reported shape/coherence results are used; they do not validate dynamic material effects.

claims.locator: F24 Section 2; W25 Section I; T25 Figure 2; F26 publisher abstract
claims.claim: Historical systems address thumb, index and middle fingertips.
claims.allowedNarration: Three moving contact surfaces meet three fingertips.
claims.avoid: Two historical contact planes plus four transducers.

claims.claim: Grasp maps to shape, squeeze to stiffness, tilt to center-of-gravity shift, shake to inertia.
claims.avoid: All four properties have quantitatively validated perceptual equivalence.

claims.claim: Local plane orientation supplies a contact cue while vision supplies global geometry and fingertip placement.
claims.avoid: The hardware mechanically reproduces a complete arbitrary object or its full grasp aperture.

claims.claim: Participants distinguished labeled tilt patterns; intended plausibility/Stroop evidence was not supported.
claims.avoid: Universal shape realism or accurate recognition of any 3D object.

claims.claim: Grip-derived indentation controls the index/middle contour-normal tilt; thumb orientation is held fixed in this experiment.
claims.avoid: A calibrated general-purpose stiffness law or all-three-finger deformation experiment.

claims.claim: Coherence improved significantly; softness showed a nonsignificant trend.
claims.allowedNarration: The study found better agreement between what people saw and felt; the change in softness ratings was not statistically clear.
claims.avoid: A proven expanded softness range, or that better coherence directly causes softness improvement.

claims.claim: A thumb pressure sensor supplies grip input for haptic and visual stimuli; the described July apparatus has a wrist-mounted controller/battery.
claims.avoid: Three measured sensors or integrated electronics attributed specifically to the July description.

claims.claim: The September report places FSR400 sensors below the fins and uses three XC330 servos with 1:1 gears and plus/minus 45-degree contact-plane travel.
claims.avoid: The pressure-sensor mesh must rotate rigidly with its fin.

claims.claim: Unity calculates each plane's angle using hand position, pose, acceleration and fingertip force.
claims.avoid: The historical computation ran in the current AtomS3 container state pipeline.

claims.locator: Figure 1, formulas embedded in the drawing
claims.claim: The figures add grip-normalized gravity-torque and horizontal/vertical acceleration terms to baseline tilt.
claims.avoid: These figures fully specify controller gains, units, servo signs or zero-force handling.

claims.claim: In the 2D illustration, CoG and horizontal-inertia increments turn the three contacts in the same diagram-plane direction; vertical inertia opposes thumb and index/middle directions.
claims.avoid: These are calibrated positive/negative servo commands or historical common/differential channel names.

claims.claim: CoG and inertia are demonstrated/proposed effects; no isolated quantitative perceptual validation is supplied.
claims.avoid: A measured equivalent mass, validated fluid response, or free-space whole-hand force reproduction.

claims.claim: FresnelShape improved reported visual-haptic coherence across the tested shapes.
claims.avoid: These scores validate stiffness, center of gravity or inertia.

claims.claim: Circle contrast survived correction; triangle contrast did not.
claims.avoid: A uniform reliable effect for every shape.

sceneRecipes.example: A solid curved surface becomes three local tangent patches, then the original three-plane CAD.
sceneRecipes.disclosure: Local directions are sampled; the whole physical surface is not reconstructed.

sceneRecipes.example: Compare ball, box, bottle shoulder and indented waist with matching tangent directions.
sceneRecipes.disclosure: Broad curvature illustration, not measured microscopic bump or texture rendering.

sceneRecipes.example: Equal input gives contrasting illustrative indentation in the bottle middle versus shoulder; index/middle tilt follows the changing contour.
sceneRecipes.disclosure: Thumb remains fixed when explaining the D25 experiment; softer/harder region comparison is explanatory rather than a calibrated study result.

sceneRecipes.example: Tilt a partly filled bottle; show a virtual mass marker, offset and gravity arrow with a sustained added tilt cue.
sceneRecipes.disclosure: Virtual CoG and synthetic plane motion; no real moving ballast or measured equivalent weight.

sceneRecipes.example: Move laterally, brake and reverse, then repeat vertically with a distinct acceleration arrow.
sceneRecipes.disclosure: Cue follows acceleration rather than constant velocity; water lag and joint commands are illustrative.

sceneRecipes.example: Return to one CAD model and the four actions with dated publication cards.
sceneRecipes.disclosure: Research branches overlap; original prototypes and experiments differ.

auditNotes: Figure equations and arrows were inspected in rendered PDFs; plain text extraction misses the formulas.
Actual front-page authors override inconsistent secondary metadata.
A local file named IEEEVR_2025_HirokiOta.pdf contained an older anonymous full-paper draft with a different title; it was excluded as evidence for the published VRW two-page paper.
The broader institutional softness summary is qualified by the narrower D25 manuscript statistics.
A CAD document name establishes design provenance, not exact equivalence to each published photographed prototype.
No primary paper in this ledger validates the current two-plane/four-vibration implementation.
